cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to believers (2 Peter 1:1). He just reminded them that the prophets spoke from God, carried along by the Holy Spirit (2 Peter 1:21). Now he turns a corner: back in the day, there were also false prophets among the people.

cards.question: False prophets showed up among God's people long ago. What does Peter warn the believers they'll have among them?

cards.text: Peter says these false teachers will bring in destructive heresies.

cards.question: Peter says the false teachers will bring in their heresies out in the open where everyone can see them coming.
These false teachers go so far as to deny someone. Who does Peter say they deny?

cards.text: Peter says where that road ends. They'll bring swift destruction on themselves.

cards.question: Peter says only a handful of people will follow these false teachers.
Many will follow the false teachers. What does Peter say happens to the way of truth because of them?
In their ___, these false teachers will exploit the believers with deceptive words.

cards.text: Peter says the longstanding verdict against them still stands, and their destruction does not sleep.
Now Peter builds his case with a string of ifs, like a lawyer laying out exhibits. Exhibit A: the angels who sinned.

cards.question: What did God do with the angels who sinned?

answers.text: Cast them into hell in chains of darkness
Sent them out to wander the earth in exile
Set them to guard the way to Eden's tree

cards.text: Exhibit B: the ancient world. God did not spare it when He brought the flood on its ungodly people.

cards.question: God didn't spare the ancient world, but He preserved ___, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight.

cards.text: Exhibit C: the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. God condemned them to destruction and reduced them to ashes.

cards.question: Why does Peter say God reduced Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes?

answers.text: As an example of what is coming on the ungodly
As a warning to the king of Egypt
To make room for the tribes of Israel

cards.text: Exhibit D, and this one's different. God rescued Lot, a righteous man living right in the middle of all that.

cards.question: Peter says Lot was tormented in his righteous soul by the lawless deeds he saw and heard.

cards.text: All those ifs are stacked up like cookie boxes on a shelf, friend. Now Peter tells us what they add up to.

cards.question: After all those examples, what does Peter say the Lord knows how to do?

answers.text: Rescue the godly and hold the unrighteous for punishment
Keep the godly from ever facing any trials
Spare the unrighteous if a few godly remain

cards.text: Peter says the punishment on the day of judgment is specially reserved for a certain kind of person: those who indulge the corrupt desires of the flesh and despise authority.

cards.question: Peter describes those who despise authority as timid and careful about who they speak against.
The false teachers boldly slander glorious beings. What about the angels, who are greater in strength and power?

answers.text: They don't dare bring such slanderous charges
They bring even harsher charges of their own
They take the false teachers' side

cards.text: Peter says these men are like irrational animals, creatures of instinct, born to be captured and destroyed.

cards.question: Like creatures of instinct, the false teachers blaspheme. What does Peter say about the matters they blaspheme in?

cards.text: Peter says the harm coming to them is the result of their own wickedness.

cards.question: Peter says the false teachers keep their carousing hidden until after dark.
Peter calls the false teachers blots and blemishes, reveling in their deception. When does he say they do it?

answers.text: As they feast with the believers
As they pray with the believers
As they sing with the believers

cards.text: Peter keeps going. Their eyes are full of adultery, and their desire for sin is never satisfied.

cards.question: Peter says the false teachers go after people who are steady and firm in the faith.

cards.text: Peter calls them accursed children with hearts trained in greed. They've left the straight way and wandered off to follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, whose story is in Numbers (Numbers 22:5).

cards.question: The false teachers follow the way of Balaam son of Beor. What did Balaam love?

cards.text: But Balaam got rebuked for his transgression. And friend, you are NOT going to believe who did the rebuking.

cards.question: Balaam the prophet was rebuked for his transgression by a ___.

cards.text: A donkey that couldn't talk spoke with a man's voice and restrained the prophet's madness. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer next to a pile of dead batteries, friend, and not ONE of them ever talked me out of anything.
Peter calls these men springs without water and mists driven by a storm. A spring without water is a big cookie box with a fancy bow on top and NOTHING inside.

cards.question: Peter says blackest darkness is reserved for the false teachers.

cards.text: With lofty but empty words, the false teachers appeal to the sensual passions of the flesh.

cards.question: With their lofty but empty words, who do the false teachers try to entice?

answers.text: Those just escaping people who live in error
Those who have walked with Jesus for years
Those who have never heard of Jesus at all

cards.text: And here's their big sales pitch to those people. They promise them freedom.

cards.question: The false teachers promise freedom, while they themselves are ___ to depravity.
Peter says a man stays free no matter what has mastered him.

cards.text: Now Peter looks at a sad turn. What if people have escaped the corruption of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome by it again?

cards.question: What does Peter say about the final condition of those who escape and then get entangled again?

answers.text: It is worse than it was at first
It is the same as it was before
It is better for having escaped once

cards.text: Peter says it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to know it and then turn away from the holy commandment passed on to them.
Peter wraps up with two proverbs he says are true of them. The first one: “A dog returns to its vomit.”

cards.question: Peter's second proverb is about a sow that has been washed. What does it say she does?

answers.text: Goes back to wallowing in the mud
Stays clean and away from the mud
Runs off into the open field
